result.topic_en: Draft notes on representing a rational function on the algebraic curve F(s,z)=0 as a quotient of polynomials whose zero sets vary with fixed residual intersections, and on how this gives the general solution of Abel's differential equations sum dw = 0 (the Jacobi inversion setting with p and 2p-2 points).

methods.what: Points where a rational function takes a given value are the common roots of F(s,z)=0 and chi - rho psi = 0, with rho = chi/psi
Varying the coefficients of f while keeping the remaining common roots fixed moves the m points as the level sets of a rational function
methods.quote: dann die Coefficienten in derselben so ändern lässt, dass die übrigen gemeinschaftlichen Wurzeln [-...-] constant bleiben

methods.what: For m >= p+1 a rational function can be written as a quotient of two adjoint polynomials phi
methods.quote: Wenn $m \geqq p+1$, kann $\varrho$ in die Form $\frac{\varphi^{(1)}}{\varphi^{(2)}}$ dargestellt werden

methods.what: Abel's differential relations for points moving in a linear system
General solution of sum over 2p-1 points of dw = 0 via zeros of a linear combination of the p adjoint polynomials (2p-2 zeros of a differential)
methods.quote: $\varphi = \alpha_1\varphi^{(1)} + \alpha_2\varphi^{(2)} + \dots + \alpha_p\varphi^{(p)} = 0$ oder die $2p-2$ Werthenpaare, für welche $dw$ unendlich klein von der zweiten Ordnung

methods.what: The sum of the integrals over the 2p-2 zeros of a differential is congruent to a constant system
Abel's theorem: the sums of the integrals over the level set of a rational function are congruent to a constant system
